definition: Inkling is an open-weights large language model created by Thinking Machines company, first released on July 15, 2026.
details: It is published under an Apache 2.0 license. The model allows text, images and audio as input, and can be used for tasks such as chat, software development, multilingual applications or agentic systems.

explainer.lead: Inkling is an open-weights large language model from Thinking Machines, first released July 15, 2026. It matters as an openly licensed multimodal model usable for chat, coding, multilingual and agentic work.

tiers.eli5: Like a publicly available brain you can download and use for talking, coding, translating or automating tasks.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can use it for tasks such as chat, software development, multilingual applications or agentic systems, feeding it text, images and audio. A pitfall is assuming open weights guarantee suitability without evaluating on your task.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-weights large language model under Apache 2.0 accepting text, images and audio as input; its known limits are not otherwise specified.

explainer.example: A team deploys Inkling to power a multilingual chat assistant that also accepts screenshots as input.
